relations.myth: Creation and delegation of worldly domains
relations.note: Bondye creates or empowers the lwa and delegates worldly domains to them.
Some practitioners describe the lwa as Bondye’s servants, emissaries, or subordinate agents.
relations.source: Desmangles, The Faces of the Gods

relations.note: Some accounts call the Marasa Bondye’s earliest creations or first children.
Lineage-specific formulations metaphorically describe the Marasa as Bondye’s first children.
Some later interpretations call Danbala Bondye’s first creation or eldest servant.
Christian-Vodou discourse variably presents Jesus as Bondye’s divine Son and savior.
Mary intercedes before Bondye through Catholic prayer incorporated into Vodou practice.
Saints intercede before Bondye and may serve as counterparts or faces of lwa.
Scholars and practitioners comparatively equate both as supreme creators above active spirits.
Haitian practice often directly identifies Bondye with the Christian God.
Variable Christian-influenced discourse places Satan beneath Bondye’s ultimate sovereignty.
The just creator supporting the enslaved is morally opposed to the enslavers’ God.
relations.source: Dumesle, Voyage dans le nord d’Hayti
